children: It's the first of the month, giving investors another look into the Chinese car business. Domestic sales are slowing while exports continue apace.

In October, Chinese EV leader BYD sold 483,125 passenger vehicles, up 11% from a year ago. Domestic sales, however, were about 310,000 units, down almost 10%. Export sales of 170,194 vehicles rose 104% compared with October 2025. Exports accounted for about 35% of total sales. Year to date, BYD has exported 1.5 million cars, up more than 90% from a year ago.

Slowing domestic Chinese sales and high production capacity have been a deadly combination for global auto makers — particularly in Europe. Coming into the week, Volkswagen stock was down 34% year to date, falling with earnings estimates. Wall Street projects 2027 operating profit of about $16 billion. A year ago, that estimate was closer to $25 billion.
High exports haven't helped BYD stock. Coming into the week, shares were down about 28% year to date.
XPeng reported October sales of 50,237 vehicles, up 20% from a year ago.
More hasn't been better though. Coming into the week, XPeng stock was down 55% year to date. XPeng is expected to lose 5 cents a share in 2027. A year ago, Wall Street projected a 55 cent profit.
Through Friday trading, XPeng stock was down about 55% year to date.
NIO reported October sales of 34,246 vehicles, up down 15% from a year ago. Li Auto reported October sales of 29,025 vehicles, down 9%.
Coming into the week. NIO and Li stocks were off 37% and 35%, respectively.
More cars, less cars, or more exports, nothing has helped Chinese cars stocks perform well so far this year.
